subject: Clarify DPA carveouts for KV-cache telemetry & subprocessor access
messages:
From: Sofia R. <sofia.r@nimbushealth.com>
To: naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@securevault.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA carveout request re: KV cache + subprocessor access

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the performance looked great. Our legal team has reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and flagged two items that will block procurement unless we get narrower language or a carveout:

1) The runtime KV-cache references and telemetry exported to some analytics subprocessors (they want assurances that user-generated content is not routed to external analytics vendors).
2) Broad "runtime access" subprocessor language — they want an exhibit listing subprocessor categories and an approval path for any new telemetry or analytics vendors.

I've attached a marked-up DPA (dpa_redline_nimbus_v3.docx). Can your product/security teams comment on the technical feasibility of the restrictions and whether those carveouts would meaningfully constrain delivery or roadmap? Procurement is asking for a proposed sign-off timeline so we can keep the September procurement window.

Appreciate any color,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ramirez
Head of Platform Integrations, Nimbus Health
sofia.r@nimbushealth.com

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: DPA carveout request re: KV cache + subprocessor access

Team — forwarding Nimbus' redlines. They want two concrete changes: limit telemetry routing to internal analytics or named vendors, and an approval path for new subprocessors touching runtime telemetry/KV snapshots.

Quick asks:
- Olga (Security): are we comfortable with a narrow carveout that states "no customer content is sent to external analytics; only anonymized runtime metrics may be shared with named vendors"? Any redlines you'd insist on?
- Karthik (Product): what's the product/ops impact if we promise a named-vendor-only telemetry routing + an approval SLA for new vendors? Would that block features in the next quarter?

Procurement expects a proposed path by EOD Friday so Nimbus can finalize PO. I attached their redline and a KV cache diagram I pulled from the infra doc.

Thanks — Naomi

--
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA carveout request re: KV cache + subprocessor access

Naomi — thanks for the ping and the redline. High level: security prioritizes minimal exposure to third-party analytics vendors for any runtime data that could be reconstructed or correlated. My read and recommendations below.

Quoted from Nimbus redline: "Provider may export runtime telemetry and KV-cache snapshots to third-party analytics subprocessors for product improvements" — this is too broad.

Proposed security language (summary):
- Replace the above sentence with: "Provider will not route raw or reconstructable customer content to any external analytics subprocessor. Provider may share aggregate, differential, or synthetic telemetry limited to system performance metrics (latency, error rates, token counts) with named, contract-approved vendors. Any telemetry that could be tied to customer inputs (prefixes, KV keys, model outputs) is excluded from external routing."
- We should require an exhibit listing current named analytics subprocessors and a notification window (30 days) plus an approval escalation to Customer Security for any new vendor that would receive telemetry beyond system-level metrics.
- For the KV-cache: we must explicitly state that KV snapshots containing customer content are either never persisted externally or are stored only in provider-controlled encrypted storage and not transmitted to analytics subprocessors.

Operational impact notes for Product/Infra:
- We can reasonably implement named-vendor routing for telemetry; it requires a short lifecycle gating (config flag + manifest) and a small infra change to enforce the manifest at export time. This work is scoped at ~2 dev-weeks (infra + QA) if we prioritize it.
- Preventing KV snapshot export to analytics is already the default for most runtime flows; I want the product team to confirm that there isn't an edge path (legacy batch export) that still sends snapshots out.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Product confirms the absence or work estimate for any legacy export paths.
2) Legal drafts the proposed replacement language and the named-subprocessor exhibit approach.
3) Security will prepare a brief threat-model note for Nimbus security if they need it.

I can sign off on the replacement language above once product confirms the infra effort and the PM/infra assignee.

- Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA carveout request re: KV cache + subprocessor access

Naomi / Olga — quick product note. We do have a legacy batch export path used by one analytics partner (historical usage metrics) that can include aggregate KV usage stats. It does not include raw customer content, but I want to be explicit:

- Current state: live runtime does not stream customer content to external analytics. Historical batch exports can include anonymized KV metrics; those exports are gated behind a scheduled job that runs from an internal bucket.
- Effort to comply: we can (a) disable the legacy batch export for this customer and (b) add a manifest-based enforcement to the export pipeline to ensure only named vendors get aggregate-only data. Disabling and gating is ~1.5 dev-weeks plus one week of QA/validation. If we want to add a 30-day vendor notification + customer approval escalation flow, that'll require additional small product UI work and a formal sign-off path (~2 more dev-weeks).

Recommendation for procurement timeline: if Security's replacement language is acceptable, we can produce an internal change request and route the infra work as a P1 to meet Nimbus' September window — doable if we start tomorrow and prioritize. Otherwise, request a narrow exception window in the contract (30 days after PO) so we can complete the gating.

Happy to jump on a 20-min sync with Nimbus' security to walk through the threat model.

— Karthik

--
